Documentation → Devices & Lifecycle → Capacity Limits

Capacity Limits

See Fortinet's factory limit for every object type of every FortiWeb you manage — server policies, protection profiles, certificates, SNI, server pools, virtual servers and virtual IPs — and set your own safety limit as a number or a percent of it — or one default percent for every row at once; clone, deploy and Plugin Studio workflows and device health check the effective limit before objects are created.

👤 ForAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereFortiWeb or FortiADC ADOM → Administrator → Capacity Limits (URL /capacity/)

What is it?#

Capacity Limits shows, for every FortiWeb you manage, how many objects of each kind it can hold: Fortinet's factory limit for its model and firmware build, and your own limit below it. SATOM's clone, deploy and Plugin Studio workflows check the lower of the two before they create objects, and device health grades how close each appliance is to it.

What does it do?#

  • Lists every registered FortiWeb on its own, grouped by platform and firmware major — FortiWeb-VM · 8.0, FortiWeb-1000F · 7.6. The platform is what Fortinet publishes limits for; the model string the box prints (FortiWeb-KVM 8.0.6) is not used as a key.
  • Shows, per object type:
Column What it is
In use How many the device holds now, from SATOM's cache (one value per device when the group has several)
Fortinet limit The factory maximum, with the build it is for and where it comes from (Max Value API or admin guide)
Your limit Fortinet limit (no buffer) — or default ( %) when a default limit is set — a number, or a percent of Fortinet limit
Effective The lowest of them — the number automations respect
  • Takes a Default limit per product: one percent of the Fortinet limit that every row without a limit of its own uses, rows that appear later (a new device, firmware or planned model) included.
  • Object types: Server Policies, Web Protection Profiles (inline), Web Protection Profiles (offline), Local Certificates, SNI Policies, Server Pools, Virtual Servers, Virtual IPs.
  • Counts each type where Fortinet counts it: per appliance (server policies, server pools, virtual IPs — every ADOM of the box together) or per ADOM (protection profiles, certificates, SNI, virtual servers).
  • Is checked by:
  • the clone/migrate pre-flight checklist of a server policy (see Policy cloning);
  • the clone and re-bind of a Web Protection Profile from Exceptions and Attack search, for every object type of the whole clone plan;
  • Plugin Studio's Pick a FortiWeb by capacity;
  • Device health, which grades each object type against the effective limit.

Where the factory limits come from#

Fortinet's published maximums travel in SATOM's signed knowledge and API packs, like the release notes: a connected SATOM receives them on its own, an isolated one with the next update package or a pack upload (Admin → Software Update → Knowledge packs). They are collected from Fortinet's Max Value Table (docs.fortinet.com/max-value-table) and from Appendix B: Maximum configuration values of the FortiWeb administration guide, per exact firmware build.

  • A build with no data of its own uses the nearest build of the same major (marked nearest build); never another major, because limits move between majors.
  • Where Fortinet's two sources disagree, the cell is marked Fortinet's two sources disagree on this cell and the Max Value Table's number is used.

FortiWeb-VM#

A FortiWeb-VM's limits are not a fixed number: Fortinet ties them to the VM's memory.

Object type Fortinet's rule for FortiWeb-VM
Server policies 20 for the first GB of RAM + 15 per extra GB, at most 256; 1024 from 64 GB
Server pools 256 below 64 GB; 1024 from 64 GB
Others the value of every other platform, where Fortinet gives one

SATOM evaluates the rule on the memory of the VM's last hardware scan (MemTotal, rounded down to whole GB, as Fortinet specifies). The hourly device sync rescans a FortiWeb when its last scan is missing or older than a week; Monitoring → Hardware scan does it on demand. A VM never scanned shows depends on the VM's memory: run a hardware scan and nothing is blocked.

Requirements#

  • The appliance's Model and Firmware must be known in Appliances.
  • Counts come from SATOM's local cache of the appliance's objects, so the appliance must have been synchronised at least once.
  • Factory limits need a knowledge or API pack that carries them, imported on a SATOM that reads them (the release after 3.5.0 and later).

Permissions#

All routes (view, add, save, delete, default limit, apply to all) require users.manage (Administrator). Without it, /capacity/ answers 403, and the menu entry is not shown.

Where it is reachable. The menu entry Capacity Limits is in the Administrator group of the FortiWeb and FortiADC ADOMs. The URL also opens in the Global, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs. Each product ADOM shows its own product's catalogs; Global shows every product's.

How to use#

Set one limit for everything#

  1. Open Administrator → Capacity Limits.
  2. In the Default limit card, enter a percent next to the product — for example 80 — and press Save. Empty = off.
  3. Every row whose Your limit is default (80 %) now uses 80 % of its Fortinet limit; Effective shows the number on each row (50 → 40). Rows that appear later inherit it.
  4. A row with its own number or percent keeps it. To put every row on the default, press Apply to all rows () and confirm: it clears the own number/percent of those n rows. An Override of the Fortinet number stays — it changes the base the percent applies to, not the limit.

Under the field, the card shows where monitoring will warn: the warning level of the Thresholds page is a percent of the effective limit, so with both at 80 % the warning appears at 64 % of the Fortinet limit.

Set your limit#

  1. Open Administrator → Capacity Limits. Every FortiWeb of the ADOM already has its card.
  2. For each object type, choose Your limit: - Fortinet limit — no buffer, the factory limit applies (shown as default ( %) when a default limit is set: the default applies); - number — an absolute limit, for example 200; - percent of Fortinet limit — for example 80 keeps 20 % free.
  3. Press Save ().
  4. Check Effective — the number automations will respect, per device.

Override Fortinet's number#

Only when Fortinet's number is wrong for a box (a licence tier the model string does not show, for instance):

  1. Open Override under the Fortinet limit.
  2. Enter the real ceiling and save. Your percent now applies to the override.

Plan a model you do not have#

  1. Enter it under Plan a model without a device (e.g. FortiWeb-1000F), pick the Product and the Firmware major, and press Add model.
  2. The card shows the factory limits of the newest build of that major. A planned card with no device can be removed with its trash button.

Example#

🧪Example — Keep 20 % free on the lab VMs

{device}, {device} and {device} are FortiWeb-VMs with 3,726 MB of RAM — 3 GB by Fortinet's rounding. Fortinet's rule gives them 20 + 2 × 15 = 50 server policies.

Object type In use Fortinet limit Your limit Effective
Server Policies 50 50 · 8.0.6 · Max Value API percent of Fortinet limit 80 40

A clone onto {device} is blocked with "Capacity limit reached for Server Policies on {device}: used 50 + 1 would exceed cap 40 (Fortinet's limit 50)."

Result#

  • Saving updates only rows that changed and stamps them with your user name; the page shows "Saved limit row(s)." or "No changes.".
  • The Audit log records capacity.model_add, capacity.limits_update, capacity.model_delete, capacity.default_set (old → new percent) and capacity.default_apply (rows reset).
  • From then on:
  • a create that would exceed the effective limit is blocked with "Capacity limit reached for on : used + would exceed cap (Fortinet's limit ).";
  • an object type with no known limit never blocks work: "No capacity limit set for / ; allowing (used=).";
  • Device health grades each object type by percentage of the effective limit (defaults 80 % and 95 %).

Troubleshooting#

A device shows "holds > : not enforced — set your own limit"#

Possible causes - The device already holds more objects than Fortinet's published limit. The box itself proves it accepts more (an older build, a licence tier), so SATOM does not block on that number.

Solution 1. If you want a ceiling anyway, set Your limit as a number, or enter an Override.

Verification - Effective shows your number.

The Fortinet limit says "depends on the VM's memory: run a hardware scan"#

Possible causes - The FortiWeb-VM has never been hardware-scanned, so SATOM does not know its RAM.

Solution 1. Run Monitoring → Hardware scan, or wait for the next hourly sync.

Verification - The Fortinet limit shows a number and GB of RAM.

The Fortinet limit says "no factory limits for this build yet"#

Possible causes - No knowledge or API pack carrying capacity limits has been imported, or none covers that firmware major.

Solution 1. Admin → Software Update → Knowledge packs: import the newest pack, or upload it on an isolated install.

Verification - The column shows a number with its build and source.

"The default limit must be a percent greater than 0 and at most 100"#

Possible causes - The default limit field holds 0, a value above 100 or text.

Solution 1. Enter a percent such as 80, or leave the field empty to turn the default off.
